literal_replacements.from:
in claude code:

```bash
/plugin marketplace add cursor/plugins
/plugin install pstack@cursor-plugins
```

claude code prefixes plugin commands and agents, so `/poteto-mode` is `/pstack:poteto-mode`. the [claude code adapter](./docs/harness/claude-code.md) maps every other cursor name. in claude code, `/pstack:setup-pstack` writes your model choices to `~/.claude/rules/pstack-models.md`, and a step that needs a cursor-only feature, such as bugbot or automations, is skipped with a one-line note.

claude code installs a generated copy of pstack, including this readme and the guide, from [`harness/pstack/`](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/tree/main/harness/pstack) at the repository root. after you change pstack, run `node scripts/generate-pstack-harness-trees.mjs` from the repository root and commit the result. ci fails while the generated copy is out of date.
literal_replacements.reason: Drop the upstream Claude Code install path; it installs the Cursor package, not this port.

literal_replacements.from: out of the box the mode splits work by model strength: code delegates (feature, refactoring, bug fix, perf, hillclimb) go to grok, while the hardest changes, prose, and judgment go to opus 5.5. the default panel is opus 5.5 / grok.
literal_replacements.to: out of the box the mode splits work by role: code delegates (feature, refactoring, bug fix, perf, hillclimb) use the configured fast model, while the hardest changes, prose, and judgment use the configured judgment model. the default panel pairs the judgment and fast models.

literal_replacements.from:
Whether `/poteto-mode` stays on depends on how the user starts it:

- Enter on `/poteto-mode` attaches the skill to one message. It fades as the chat moves on.
- Option+Enter on Mac or Alt+Enter on Windows, or Use as Mode from the skill entry, makes it a Custom Mode. It stays in context every turn until the user exits the mode, and it stays out of casual turns.
- Cursor's docs list Custom Modes in the Agents Window and the CLI. Elsewhere, start each new task with `/poteto-mode`.
literal_replacements.to: To keep `/poteto-mode` on, start each new task with it.
literal_replacements.reason: Custom Modes are a Cursor feature.

literal_replacements.from: **(b) Apply it.** Build the working table from the skill defaults, and on a re-run keep any role you changed by family, list, or alias (`inherit-parent`, `auto`). `unlimited`, `large`, `medium`, and `small` set the effort token of every real slug, panel entries included, to `max`, `xhigh`, `high`, or `medium`. The effort token is the last token, or the one before a trailing `fast`, on the ladder `max` > `xhigh` > `high` > `medium` > `low`. If the result is not a detected slug, use the same family's detected slug with the highest effort at or below the target, else mark the role as needing a choice. `inherit-parent` and `auto` do not change. So `unlimited` turns `claude-opus-5-5-xhigh` into `claude-opus-5-5-max`. Grok slugs top out at `xhigh`, so under `unlimited` the fallback puts Grok at `xhigh` and keeps `grok-4.7-xhigh-fast` as it is. `large` keeps both defaults. `small` turns them into `claude-opus-5-5-medium` and `grok-4.7-medium-fast`.
literal_replacements.to: **(b) Apply it.** Build the working table from the skill defaults, and on a re-run keep any role you changed by model, list, or alias (`inherit-parent`, `auto`). `unlimited`, `large`, `medium`, and `small` set the `reasoning_effort` of every role with a real model, panel entries included, to `max`, `xhigh`, `high`, or `medium`, on the ladder `max` > `xhigh` > `high` > `medium` > `low`. If a model does not support the target effort, use its highest supported effort at or below the target, else mark the role as needing a choice. `inherit-parent` and `auto` do not change. `large` keeps the defaults.
literal_replacements.reason: Codex sets reasoning effort in a TOML field instead of a slug suffix.
